Where This Could Go

Where This Could Go
There are a lot of directions we could take this. The goal is to help both founders and job seekers, and a handful of products out there have really inspired us.
For job seekers
career-ops
(opens in a new tab)
is an open-source job search agent that runs in your terminal. It scores each job against your CV and tailors your resume, and you still press Submit.
Tsenta
(opens in a new tab)
is an AI career agent that finds roles that fit and applies for you.
For both sides
Jack & Jill
(opens in a new tab)
gives each side of the market its own AI agent. Jack works for the job seeker, Jill works for the company, and together they make the introduction.
For founders
Juicebox
(opens in a new tab)
and
Paraform
(opens in a new tab)
help founders hit their hiring goals: Juicebox with AI search and sourcing agents, Paraform by putting their hardest roles in front of a network of expert recruiters.
And a nod to
gstack
(opens in a new tab)
. It has nothing to do with hiring, but it is genuinely useful to builders, and that kind of usefulness builds a brand people want to work with.

01 · The role
What Is a Founding Engineer?
A founding engineer is one of the first engineers at a startup, usually somewhere in the first five hires, brought on before the product has proven itself. The work is not a slice of a system; it is the system. You ship version one of everything, own whatever breaks, make the architecture calls that stick for years, and interview the engineers who come after you.
It is not a founder role. Founders hold founder stock and take the cap-table risk; a founding engineer is the earliest kind of employee, with a real salary plus an options grant that is large by employee standards and small by founder standards. The trade is deliberate: less cash than a big company would pay, more ownership and more surface area than a big company could ever offer.
The "founding" prefix has also spread past engineering. On this board right now there are 82 founding-titled roles: 38 in engineering, plus founding account executives, founding designers, founding recruiters, and first hires of most other crafts. The chart below covers all of them, and you can filter down to engineering in one click.

Everything the jobs board knows, readable by machines: live open roles across the
speedrun
and a16z portfolios, hiring companies, curated collections, and aggregate comp data. Two doors, same data, same freshness. No auth, no keys, no cost.
01 · REST API
/api/v1
Versioned JSON over HTTPS at
https://speedrun-talent-network.com/api/v1
. Read-only. Open CORS, so it works straight from a browser or an agent runtime. Responses are edge-cached for 1 to 5 minutes. The spec at
/api/v1/openapi.json
is complete and accurate to the implementation.
Endpoint
What it returns
GET /api/v1/jobs
Search open roles: q, fn, spec, sen, lvl, emp, loc, metro, wp (remote | hybrid | onsite), comp, comp_max, comp_any, posted (24h | 7d | 30d), stage, size, industry, lab, bigtech, portfolio, cohort, company, stealth, scope (speedrun | portfolio | everywhere), sort, page. Returns jobs + live facet counts + total.
GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}
One role: full description text, posted pay band, how to apply. Closed roles return status:"closed".
GET /api/v1/companies
Every portfolio company with at least one live role, most open roles first.
GET /api/v1/companies/{slug}
Company profile + all of its live roles.
GET /api/v1/collections
Curated collections: portfolio tiers, core industries, hubs, investors, signals. Live counts.
GET /api/v1/collections/{slug}
One collection with ranked member companies.
GET /api/v1/stats/hiring
Aggregate hiring data: demand mix, posted pay bands by function, remote share, top cities.
GET /api/v1/openapi.json
The complete OpenAPI 3.1 spec.
Try it:
curl "https://speedrun-talent-network.com/api/v1/jobs?fn=engineering&loc=remote&comp=200000&source=my-agent"
Errors come back as
{"error":{"code","message"}}
with a matching HTTP status.
Every list is capped and paginated; responses carry
page
,
page_size
,
total_pages
. Job searches also carry
has_more
and
next_page
: stop paging when
has_more
is false (pages s
